title.narrative: Increased awareness to stakeholders on climate change impact in World Heritage sites and support Member State to prepare nomination file for submission to the World Heritage Centre through the upstream process

description.narrative:
Climate change has become one of the most significant threats to World Heritage, impacting the Outstanding Universal Values (OUV), integrity and authenticity, of many properties and economic and social development and quality of life of communities connected with World Heritage properties. Therefore, it is important to be at the forefront of exploring and managing the impacts of climate change on World Heritage through increasing awareness to different stakeholders so that they can take immediate action.
Strengthen capacity of World Heritage Site Managers to adapt and/or mitigate to the impacts of climate: World Heritage properties harbour options for society to mitigate and adapt to climate change through the ecosystem benefits, such as water and climate regulation, that they provide and the carbon that is stored in World Heritage forest sites. Also, World Heritage properties serve as climate change observatories to gather and share information on applied and tested monitoring, mitigation and adaptation practices.
Build capacity of Youth Conservation Ambassadors in protection and conservation of World Heritage site: As part of the recently completed project titled "Empowering young women and men for climate change adaptation at the Kilimanjaro World Heritage site", 18 youth were selected to be Youth Conservation Ambassadors. They are working closely with the authorities and their communities in the protection of the site. There is a need to continuous build their capacity so that they are well equipped to protect the site accordingly.
